title: Acceptance cases count only by their exact result, and a worker's change to them is sent back
objective: The issuer treats a ticket's acceptance cases as passed only when each one failed outright on the code before the change, passed outright on the ticket branch, and (from round 2 on) is still defined exactly as the verifier wrote it.
outline: scripts/adapter-unittest.py: `addExpectedFailure` records `xfail`; `STATUSES`, `RANK`, docstring. scripts/testiface.py `check_result`: add `xfail` to the status tuple (line ~236), and to the docstring where it lists statuses. Leave scripts/status.py `load_result` alone: dead code that improvement-plan item 6.2 removes; nothing in devloop or scripts/testiface.py calls it. devloop/ticket_issuer.py: (1) `red_check`: after the `errors` block add the third outcome; keep its final `return None` and the blank line after it unchanged (ticket #163 in g19 edits `hard_block()` right below; one unchanged line between the hunks keeps that merge clean). (2) `run_cases`: on GREEN, check the mark rows with `case_mark(self.id)` and the same `mark in str(r.get("id"))` test red_check uses. (3) `case_definitions(git, rev, mark)` as a module function next to `case_mark`; read each file with `git show <rev>:<path>` through the Git helper; strip the `<rev>:` prefix git grep puts on each line (pass a resolved sha, not a branch name). (4) `_round`: note at the top whether `cases.run` was recorded at round start (the `t` argument, where `need_cases` is computed); insert the comparison right after the block that merges `cases["branch"]` into the ticket branch, leaving the blank line before `self.hard_block(g)` and that line itself unchanged (#163 edits that call). A helper for 'a revised event after the last round start' can sit next to `brief_revised` / `cases_thrown_out` (same loop shape, any revised event). Add the step to the module docstring's step list. devloop/prompts/verifier.md: the A5 sentence inside step 1, after the paragraph about the mark. Docs per A9. Measured 2026-11-28 on HEAD 4797416 (scratch copy, the repo's loop harness and fakes): expectedFailure is recorded as `pass` with message `expected failure`; a run with a skip row exits 0; a verifier-side skip lands in round 1; worker-side skip and no-mark rows land; an xfail row is refused by the interface (`could not measure: testiface: unmeasured: result.json ids are not a list of {id, status}`); a round-2 worker edit of the case class body, and an appended same-named class, land on main; `git grep -l -F` prints `<sha>:<path>` per file and exits 1 when nothing matches; `ast.dump` of a class is equal after moving it and adding comments, and two same-named classes give two entries. Out of scope: case files in other languages (only .py is compared); module-level helpers or fixtures without the mark (the A5 sentence steers helpers into the class); changes made to the cases from another module at run time; the fixer's case edits on integration branches (its own rules).
notes: Source: improvement plan phase one, group 4 item 4.1 (D-100, D-102); external audit finding (P0-2/P0-3/P0-6/P1-6 cover group 4) confirmed by the main session reading the code; T main session agreed 2026-11-26. Group: new-g1, one new group with the other two tickets of group 4, as the request asks; the open groups g18 (dispatch) and g19 (hard_block approval) hold unrelated work. hard_block: the project stops a ticket before merge when any added line (code, tests, comments, docs) matches `os\.kill`, `killpg`, `pkill` or `kill -`. Nothing here needs those words. The fakes in tests_devloop/fake_tests.py and fake_agent.py are the verifier's (named in the test plan); the implementer writes no fake change. #147 (stuck) may later edit scripts/testiface.py elsewhere; the change here to check_result's status tuple is one line.
acceptance: A1 Adapter: `python3 scripts/adapter-unittest.py run <ids>` on a test method decorated with `@unittest.expectedFailure` whose body fails writes that id's row in result.json with status `xfail` and message `expected failure` (today: status `pass`, measured), and exits 0 when no row is fail or error. `xfail` is added to `STATUSES` and to `RANK` (rank 1, like skip). An expectedFailure method whose body passes stays status `fail`, message `unexpected success` (unchanged).

A2 Test interface: `scripts/testiface.py` accepts `xfail` as a row status in result.json (the status tuple in the `ids` check of `check_result`, today `("pass", "fail", "error", "skip")`), so a `run` whose command exits 0 with pass/skip/xfail rows is green (rc 0) instead of unmeasured (rc 2). xfail is not a red status: only fail/error rows go with rc 1 (unchanged).

A3 Red check (`Issuer.red_check`): every result row whose id contains the ticket's mark `T<id>Acceptance` must have status exactly `fail`. The existing outcomes keep their texts and their order: `pass` rows -> 'these cases already pass before the change...', `error` rows -> 'these cases fail with an error instead of their assertion...', no mark row -> 'no acceptance case named ...'. Any other status of a mark row (`skip`, `xfail`, anything else) now sends the cases back to the verifier like the other red-check outcomes (the worker's hand-in stands), with a text containing `did not fail on the code before the change` and each such row as `<id> (<status>)`, e.g. `case_1.T1Acceptance.test_it (skip)` (up to 10). Today a skip row is accepted (measured: a ticket whose case skips lands in round 1).

A4 Case runs (`Issuer.run_cases`, at step 5 and after `integrate()` takes in the target): the verifier's cases count as passed only when the run is green AND at least one row's id contains the mark AND every row whose id contains the mark has status exactly `pass`. Otherwise the round ends unmerged and counted (no `free` on its feedback event) with feedback `verifier cases: no acceptance case named <mark> ran` when no row carries the mark, else `verifier cases: these cases did not pass: <id> (<status>), ...` (up to 10). Rows without the mark keep today's rule (only fail/error make the run red); env and unmeasured runs keep today's handling. Today a worker-side skip or a run with no mark row lands (measured).

A5 `devloop/prompts/verifier.md` step 1 gains the sentence `Helpers that only this ticket's cases use go inside the {case_mark} class, not at module level: from round 2 on devloop compares the {case_mark} definitions on the implementer's branch with yours.` Rendered with `agents.render("verifier.md", {"case_mark": "T7Acceptance"})`, the text between `\n1. ` and `\n2. ` contains `Helpers that only this ticket's cases use go inside the T7Acceptance class`.

A6 New module function `ticket_issuer.case_definitions(git, rev, mark)` (git: a `core.gitx.Git`; rev: a commit sha; mark: e.g. `T7Acceptance`) returns a dict `{(path, name): [dump, ...]}`: for each `.py` file at `rev` whose text contains `mark` (as `git grep -l -F <mark> <rev> -- '*.py'` lists them; rc 1 means none and gives `{}`), path repo-relative, every `ast.ClassDef`, `ast.FunctionDef` and `ast.AsyncFunctionDef` node yielded by `ast.walk(ast.parse(source))` whose `name` contains `mark`, as `ast.dump(node)` with default arguments (no line numbers), in `ast.walk` order. A `.py` file that contains the mark and does not parse gives the one entry `(path, None): [text]` with text starting `SyntaxError`. So moving a definition inside its file or changing comments and blank lines leaves the dict equal; changing a body, adding or removing a decorator, appending a second same-named class (a list of 2), deleting the class (key gone) or moving it to another file (another path) makes it differ; a non-.py file holding the mark gives no key.

A7 Round check: in round r >= 2 of a ticket with needs_verifier true whose `cases.run` was already recorded when the round started and whose history has no `revised` event after its last `round start`, right after the cases branch is merged into the ticket branch (step 2) and before the hard_block check, the review and the case run, the issuer compares `case_definitions` at the ticket branch HEAD with `case_definitions` at the cases branch head. When they differ, the round ends unmerged and counted (its `feedback` event has no `free`) with feedback containing `changes the verifier's acceptance cases` and, for each differing key, its path and name (up to 10), telling the worker to put them back as they are on the cases branch or hand in revise. Today a round-2 worker that edits the verifier's class body, or appends a second class of the same name to its file, lands on main (both measured).

A8 Not checked (implementer's own tests): round 1; a round that started without recorded cases (the verifier writes them in that round); a round with a `revised` event after its `round start`; a ticket with needs_verifier false. A round-2 worker that leaves the cases untouched merges as today.

A9 Docs say the same: the adapter docstring (the exit-code line `0 every id pass/skip` and the result.json section), docs/design/project-runnable-entries.md section 4 (the `run` row's exit codes and the `ids[].status` row: `pass` / `fail` / `error` / `skip` / `xfail`) and the existing devloop/README.md bullet that begins `- The verifier names every acceptance case`, extended in place (exactly fail before the change, exactly pass after, the round-2 comparison); that bullet keeps the words `result.json` and `unittest`, which MarkExplained.test_readme_bullet_explains_the_mark reads, and no other bullet before it gains `T<id>Acceptance`. Existing cases that keep passing unchanged: RedCheck (its three texts), MarkExplained (step one words; do not introduce `in Python unittest: put them in a class named`), RunWritesSchemaOne (its fixture has no expectedFailure).
token_basis: Calibrated on landed tickets #137-#161 (cache reads included): complex worker+verifier+reviewer, one round 2-4M, two rounds 5-7M. This one: ~10 small edits over 6 files (issuer red_check, run_cases, _round and a new ~30-line function; adapter 3 lines; testiface 1 line; verifier.md 1 line; 2 docs), the verifier adds 4 fake hooks and ~14 cases in two modules (loop cases 2-3 s each); a second round is likely -> 5.5M.
vision: VISION 'purpose and success metrics' (more results that pass acceptance): an acceptance result means what it says. Metric 'share passing tests the first time' becomes a true number (it may drop slightly: a skipped, expected-failure or edited case no longer counts as passed); metric 'times each ticket needs me' drops by the fix round or page a false green costs when it surfaces later. No exploit seen yet in either project, so today's measured gain is 0; it prevents one fix round or page per false green.
removes: the adapter's rule that an expected failure is a pass, and run_cases' shortcut that read rc 0 as every case passing (a skipped case counted as green)
request:
Phase one, group 4 of the improvement plan: honest acceptance and reliability (D-100, D-102). Source: external audit
P0-2, P0-3, P0-6, P1-6, each confirmed by the main session reading the code; T main session agreed (2026-11-26).
Keep these as one group, three tickets.

4.1 Acceptance results must be honest.
- Problem (read in code): a skipped acceptance case (rc 0) counts as green; `red_check()` treats skip as red but
  expectedFailure is recorded as `pass`; nothing checks whether the worker edited the `T<N>Acceptance` cases.
- Layer 1: `run_cases()` requires each case to be exactly `pass`; `red_check()` requires exactly `fail`.
  expectedFailure is recorded as `xfail` (not pass).
- Layer 2: from round 2 on, a worker change that alters the `T<N>Acceptance` definitions is sent back. Compare by
  AST (classes and functions), and check the count of same-named definitions. A round that went through `--revise`
  (the ticket was rewritten) is not a violation. The verifier prompt gets one line: helpers specific to this ticket
  go inside the class.

4.2 Controller lock uses flock.
- Problem (read in code): `PidLock` creates an empty file and then writes JSON; two `actl run` starting at once can
  both take the lock.
- Do: keep the lock file (do not delete it), use `fcntl.flock`, clear the stamp on release; `controller_alive()` and
  existing tests keep passing.

4.3 start_fixer writes once.
- Do: `start_fixer()` writes the pool once, after the spawn, and passes `--round` to `auto_fixer.py`.

vision: an acceptance result means what it says, and two controllers cannot both run.
removes: the two-write path in start_fixer; the create-then-write PidLock path.
